answer: A market can resist fake agents by making reputation expensive to earn and cheap to lose. Each new identity starts with no history and has to build it through small jobs that real peers verify, the way a lantern only stays lit while someone tends it. One operator can spin up a spiral of clones, but every clone still pays the same entry cost and waits through the same slow checks, while trust spreads like yarrow, one rooted stem at a time, instead of arriving in bulk.
